title: Ukraine's Starlink scare
deck: A week of slowed satellite links hit Ukraine's military and drones, Trump said the limits were lifted, Kyiv said they weren't, and then Kyiv said the service was back; the episode shows how much of Ukraine's war effort runs through systems Washington can influence.

fuel.title: Trump says Starlink limits lifted
fuel.how: A US presidential statement that limits were lifted, contradicted the same day by Kyiv, shows that access can turn on Washington's say-so.

fuel.title: Starlink restored as attacks continue
fuel.how: Strikes continued in both Russia and Ukraine while Kyiv reported its connection restored, so the need for reliable links never paused.

fuel.title: Le Pen pledges to cut French aid
fuel.how: If US access can be throttled and a major European donor may cut aid, European budgets face pressure to fill gaps in Ukraine's communications and support.

whatHappened: For about a week, slowed Starlink connections affected Ukraine's military and drone operations, according to BBC reporting. Our sources do not say who imposed the limits or why.
On 23 October, Trump said the limits on Starlink access had been lifted. Ukraine said the service was still restricted. Trump added that 'if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out'.

On 24 October, Ukraine said its Starlink connection was restored and 'now stable'. Attacks continued in both Russia and Ukraine. Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi next month.
whyItMatters: Politics: Trump's statement and Kyiv's contradiction on the same day show that access is shaped by decisions in Washington, not just by technology. That gives the US leverage over how Ukraine fights and negotiates. A related story, a Putin proposal for a summit with Trump and Xi, points the same way. Rubio denied any pause in US intelligence sharing.

Security: Satellite links underpin Ukrainian military communications and drone operations, and the fighting did not pause while service was degraded. A week of slow links is a real operational cost, even if the service is now reported stable. It may also push Ukraine to look for backups.

Budget: If US-controlled access can be throttled, European governments may be asked to pay for alternatives. Zelensky has answered Le Pen's pledge to cut French aid by saying lives are worth more than the price. How much Europe can and will fill the gap is uncertain, and our sources do not give figures.

predict.question: Before you read the scenarios: what is the most likely path for Ukraine's Starlink access over the next month?
options: It stays stable with no new reported limits
Access is formally tied to the peace talks
Europe fully replaces Starlink for the military
predict.explanation: Our base case, at about 50%, is that service stays stable, because Kyiv now calls it stable and Trump publicly committed to fixing problems. Repeat throttling is the next most likely path at 25%, since the cause of this episode is unexplained.

timeline.title: Starlink terminals start flowing to Ukraine
timeline.detail: Soon after Russia's full-scale invasion, Starlink service was activated for Ukraine and became a backbone for military and civilian communications. This is background from general knowledge, not from the listed sources.

timeline.title: US pauses support and, soon after, intelligence sharing
timeline.detail: After a tense Washington meeting, the US paused military aid and then intelligence sharing, resuming both within roughly two weeks. Background from general knowledge; exact dates approximate. It showed US support could be switched off quickly.

timeline.detail: He added that 'if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out'.

timeline.detail: The slowed links had affected military and drone operations for a week.

timeline.title: Attacks continue in Russia and Ukraine

scenarios.name: Restored and holds

signposts: Kyiv continues to describe service as stable
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Little lasting change, though dependency remains a talking point.

scenarios.name: Intermittent throttling returns
scenarios.looksLike: Slowdowns recur, with conflicting accounts from Washington and Kyiv each time.
signposts: Unexplained limits on specific units or regions
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Ukraine accelerates backups; trust in US reliability keeps falling.

scenarios.name: Access becomes part of the talks

signposts: US officials link access to Ukrainian concessions
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Washington's leverage over Kyiv grows; Russia gains room to press.

scenarios.name: Europe steps in quickly
scenarios.looksLike: European governments announce funded alternative links for Ukraine's military.
scenarios.effectOnWorld: Reduces US leverage but raises European defence spending and political friction over aid.

predictions.text: No new widely reported restriction on Ukrainian military Starlink access will emerge by 30 November 2026 (about 60%).
Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US will meet in Abu Dhabi by the end of November (about 65%).
US or company officials will publicly explain who imposed the limits and why (about 35%).
Ukraine or at least one European government will announce a new or expanded non-Starlink satellite or secure-communications arrangement for Ukraine's military (about 40%).
